text: In June 2018, City Council authorized the Toronto Atmospheric Fund (TAF), pursuant to the City's Relationship Framework with TAF, to receive a loan of up to $5 million and a grant of up to $750,000 from the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) for the next phase of its TowerWise Project. TowerWise supports deep energy retrofits in multi-residential buildings, aiming for a minimum of 40% reductions in greenhouse gases through the use of high-efficiency heat pump systems and other measures. At the time of Council's approval, TAF outlined a funding arrangement for the use of these funds, which included seeking additional capital from other government funding programs and potentially third-party investors. The four multi-residential buildings to be retrofitted with these funds were not yet determined. On February 5, 2021, the TAF Board of Directors approved funding of $2,841,800 net…

City Council on June 8 and 9, 2021, adopted the following: 1. City Council authorize the Toronto Atmospheric Fund loan of up to $2,841,800 net and $3,363,600 gross in the TowerWise project, subject to the terms and conditions approved by the Toronto Atmospheric Fund Board of Directors in Attachment 1 to the report (May 17, 2021) from the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer. 2. City Council direct the Toronto Atmospheric Fund to provide detailed annual reporting to the Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer on the status of this loan and the remaining loan and grant from the Federation of Canadian Municipalities. 3.
